prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Scope: acceptance–loading handoff; airline loading excluded; no explicit modes. Baggage Control System (Velvet) validates identity/current routing before disposition; applies approved screening/sort/cutoff profiles; receives Flight Cutoff Advisory; preserves assignments/holds; authorizes checked bags’ original-path return. Flight Data Gateway (Lantern) supplies timestamped flight/routing/revision/connection data, destination/service-date validation, advisory. Baggage Operations Supervisor (Tern) manages capacity/recovery/priorities; approves beyond-operator dispositions and within-window release. Security Duty Manager resolves security-release holds. Maintenance Technician isolates faults/confirms safe restart/restrictions; verifies calibration using Calibration Witness Tag before return-to-service. Concourse Zone Controller (Mosslight) manages readiness/capacity/lanes; produces Recovery Route Card; applies authorized routing without screening bypass. Staff verify eligibility/identity/flight/size/weight. Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit records/stages acceptance preserving flight; sends Oversize Exception Ticket; oversize requires approved holding/routing. Bag Tag Printer produces durable unique tags/Calibration Witness Tag; replacement requires authorized details. Transfer Bag Feeder records/meters arrivals; sends Late Transfer Bag Card; holds pending screening/onward confirmation. Induction Tray Conveyor meters scan-confirmed/spaced bags; interlocks jams/doors/downstream. North Gate Scanner (Kestrel) captures readable tag images/reads; South Gate Scanner records outcomes, produces Manual Rescan Receipt. Image Resolution Desk presents images/exceptions; uses receipt to verify approved second imaging and exception ticket for oversize position. Operator requires legible evidence, compares features/tag/handling; inconclusive images require physical inspection and attached-tag/record agreement; changed route/flight requires approval. Bag Reconciliation Station sends Bag Match Query, reconciles Late Transfer Bag Card, records flight match; mismatches held pending authorized resolution/escalation. Primary Crossbelt Sorter (Juniper) preserves identity/screening/destination, holds unresolved dispositions, sends Chute Occupancy Note; blocked chutes prohibit release. Secondary Inspection Chute controls examination/access/holds. Explosives Response Team (Pebble) examines/security-holds; produces Custody Seal Log. East Make-Up Conveyor/West Make-Up Conveyor meter assigned delivery. Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit (Orchard) preserves positions/order; receives Carousel Release Slip after position/flight checks. Outbound Load Control Desk confirms load eligibility. Airline Ramp Coordinator confirms staffing/equipment/loading sequence/flight-side acceptance

S187: The Security Duty Manager coordinates access control when a security response affects equipment or staff movement.

S189: The Maintenance Technician checks for jammed bags, damaged belts, sensor obstruction, and signs of mechanical wear before clearing a fault.
